title: The Ancient Magus' Bride: Those Awaiting a Star
summary: AniList 21688 bundles the three-part prequel OAD 魔法使いの嫁 星待つひと, which Mag Garden shipped on DVD inside the 特装版 (special edition) of manga volumes 6, 7 and 8 — Mag Garden's own product pages give 2016-09-10 (ISBN 978-4-8000-0565-6), 2017-03-10 (978-4-8000-0566-3, blurb 'アニメーションDVD中編を同梱！') and 2017-09-08 (978-4-8000-0567-0) — each disc preceded by a two-week theatrical event run (前篇 2016-08-13, 中篇 2017-02-04, 後篇 2017-08-19). It is an ORIGINAL story, not an adaptation of any printed unit: Mag Garden's own OVA site calls it 「ヤマザキコレ原案による完全オリジナルアニメーション」 and says the theatrical run reveals 「原作では描かれていない主人公チセの幼少期」 (the protagonist's childhood, WHICH IS NOT DEPICTED IN THE SOURCE); ja-WP repeats 完全オリジナルアニメーション; lisani's press write-up prints the same official copy plus the credit block (原作 ヤマザキコレ / 脚本 高羽彩); and ANN's announcement says in English 'Yamazaki wrote the original story for the anime'. The story's own cast is anime-only: on the Ancient Magus' Bride Wiki, whose character infobox carries a `Manga =` debut field (Chise Hatori reads 'Volume 1, Chapter 1'), Riichi Miura 三浦理一, Mayumi Niikura 新倉真弓 and Maho Niikura 新倉真歩 carry ONLY an `OVA =` field, and the location page Mayoiga ('Library of the Forest') has an EMPTY `manga =`; en-WP files Riichi as 'a librarian friend of Chise appeared in ... OVA'. No printed unit of the story exists in either direction — the Mag Garden / KADOKAWA bibliography holds the main manga, two spin-off manga (詩篇.75 稲妻ジャックと妖精事件, 詩篇.108 魔術師の青), two anthology novels (金糸篇 / 銀糸篇), the Supplement / Merkmal guidebooks and 断片集 1-2, whose KADOKAWA copy and contents are other short pieces (Nathan and the selkie, Theo, Alice and John; Ruth's day, Elias cooking, Renfred's familiar) — so there is no comicalization and no adoption act. Yamazaki's 原案 / 原作 is a CREDIT (T26), the work has zero standing in the instrument, and it is FILLER under T27. Structure worth recording: the childhood is told inside a PRESENT-DAY FRAME — the licensor's synopsis opens 「羽鳥チセ15歳。…エリアスに『弟子』兼『花嫁』として招き入れられた…倫敦のアンジェリカより届いた書籍を整理しようとするチセが見つけた」 and Ruth is in the frame (ANN and lisani both credit 内山昂輝 as ルツ; the wiki's Part 1 plot opens 'Chise awakens and says good morning to Ruth') — which is why the stored 0.5 is wrong as a watch position.

position.why: 0.5 was the air-date derivation (all three parts were released 2016-08-13 → 2017-09-08, before TV ep 1 on 2017-10-07) and it reads the INNER story (Chise at 8). But the work's own 'now' is the framing scene: Chise at 15, already Elias' apprentice and bride-to-be, unpacking study materials Angelica sent from London, with RUTH already her familiar (ANN and lisani credit Kōki Uchiyama as Ruth in the cast; the wiki's Part 1 plot has her greeting Ruth at Elias' house, and Part 3 closes back in that frame with Elias fetching The Legend of Tōno). Ruth is contracted and named in TV ep 8 'Let sleeping dogs lie.' (2017-11-25), so 8.5 is the earliest slot at which nothing in the frame is out of order; anything in 8.5–24.5 is equally consistent, and the precedent is one-punch-man 21386 (a prequel inside a present-day frame 'cannot sit before ep 1'). No licensor orders it before ep 1: the Shochiku SEASON1 Blu-ray BOX (SHBR-0679) files 「『魔法使いの嫁 星待つひと』三部作(前篇・中篇・後篇)」 as a 映像特典 on Disc 3, the disc that carries eps 13-18, and every streaming platform (Bandai Channel 6843/6844, Prime Video, Crunchyroll) lists it as a standalone title. Position confidence is medium — it is reasoned from the frame, not from a cited ordering.

flags_for_sean: POSITION IS THE ONLY JUDGMENT CALL HERE (standing is not close). Stored 0.5 → proposed 8.5. The three candidates and their evidence: (a) 0.5 — release order (the whole trilogy predates TV ep 1) and the inner story is Chise at 8; (b) 8.5 — the earliest episode after which the FRAME is true (Ruth is contracted and named in ep 8), the one-punch-man 21386 precedent, and no licensor ordering supports 0.5; (c) 24.5 — after the S1 finale, if you want the frame's domesticity and the mother's-suicide flashback to sit after ep 22 'As you sow, so shall you reap.', the TV run's own telling of Chise's past. I chose (b) as the earliest TRUE slot. Nothing I found is a licensor watch-order statement, so this is reasoning, not a citation — flip it freely if the halo's convention is release order.

TASK PREMISE — confirmed with three corrections of detail. (1) The discs are the 特装版 ('special edition'), not the 初回限定版 ('first limited edition') that vols 2-5 and 10-13 used — Mag Garden distinguishes the two labels. (2) The work's own run starts with the THEATRICAL event screenings (前篇 2016-08-13 — AniList's stored date; 中篇 2017-02-04; 後篇 2017-08-19), each two weeks limited in eight cinemas, with the disc following in the tankōbon. (3) The third disc's date is 2017-09-08 on Mag Garden's own product page (and on ja-WP's vol-8 line), while en-WP and the fandom both print September 9, 2017 — a one-day disagreement I could not resolve past the publisher's own page; the publisher wins.

THE ANILIST EDGE IS THE FRANCHISE TAG TRAP. The halo note ('adapts the series' own instrument: Mahoutsukai no Yome (MANGA)') comes from AniList's source:MANGA plus an ADAPTATION edge to manga 85435. Nothing of the instrument is in this work. Every AniList/MAL-style 'based on the manga' line here is the franchise credit 原作：ヤマザキコレ(マッグガーデン刊), which the OVA carries exactly as the TV series does.

DIRECTION CHECKED BOTH WAYS — there is no printed 星待つひと unit, before or after. Mag Garden's and KADOKAWA's own bibliographies list the main manga (19 vols MG / 24 vols KADOKAWA), 詩篇.75 稲妻ジャックと妖精事件 and 詩篇.108 魔術師の青 (spin-off manga, other instruments), 小説 金糸篇 / 銀糸篇 (anthology novels), Supplement I-III and Merkmal (guidebooks), and 断片集 1-2. I read the KADOKAWA copy for 断片集 1-2 specifically because a Yamazaki-drawn short would be a T26 incorporation: they collect disc- and LE-booklet shorts (Nathan and the selkie, Theo, Alice and John; the big clean, Ruth's day, Chise's dream, Elias cooking, Renfred's familiar) — no library, no Riichi. So: no comicalization, no adoption act, `adopted` stays null.

THE ONE PIECE OF SHARED GROUND, DELIBERATELY NOT COUNTED. The OVA's flashback opens on Chise's mother voicing her regret and later killing herself — and Chika Hatori IS in the manga (the wiki's debut field: Volume 4, Chapter 19 'Chise's Dream'; animated in TV ep 1's flashback and told in full in TV ep 22). No source says the OVA restages ch 19's pages rather than depicting the same background independently, so I recorded no chapter: under T28 a restaged, already-adapted beat inside an original story is a sliver with no weight anyway, and a chapter number here would be my inference, not a finding. Named so nobody re-discovers it later as a source tie.

NO TV PROLOGUE, NO RE-CUT. The 2017 TV series is 24 episodes with no ep 0 (en-WP's S1 table; the wiki's Category:Season 1 Episodes = 24 + the index page), and the OADs were not re-cut into it. What exists nearby: a スペシャルダイジェスト of cour 1 broadcast before cour 2 (ja-WP) — a recap of the TV episodes, not of this work — and the Shochiku SEASON1 Blu-ray BOX (2023-02-22, SHBR-0679), which carries 星待つひと 三部作 as a 映像特典 on Disc 3 and the 星待つひと イベント上映 footage on Disc 1.

TITLE-JOIN HAZARD: the work is written 星待つひと in the official title but 星待つ人 in several official-adjacent places (the archived mahoyome.jp STORY tab; animate's 中篇 pre-sale copy 「魔法使いの嫁 星待つ人：中篇」). Normalise both before any title join. English titles in the wild also include ANN's literal 'The Man Who Waits for Stars'.

OUT OF SCOPE, FOR THE SHELF (do not infer from this verdict): the SECOND OAD trilogy 魔法使いの嫁 西の少年と青嵐の騎士 (bundled with vols 16/17/18 特装版, 2021-09-10 / 2022-03-10 / 2022-09-09, Studio Kafka) is announced in the same words — 「ヤマザキ原案によるオリジナルアニメーション」 (ja-WP) — but I did not research it and it needs its own row; likewise the 24-part Twitter short 『まほよめ』 (collected on the vol-9 特装版 DVD) and the drama CDs on the vol-5, vol-14 and vol-20 editions.

AniList's GraphQL API returned 403 ('temporarily disabled due to severe stability issues') throughout this task. Every fact above comes from the licensor, the publishers, the two Wikipedias, the fandom API and trade press; no AniList field was re-read and no date was guessed.
